claims.claim: The pinned fork already contains an age-encrypted, OS-keyring-backed Codex secrets storage primitive with separate managed, auth, and MCP namespaces.
The accepted HostObserverV1 returns metadata and content SHA-256, not file contents, so it cannot alone supply semantic values to a pure grammar compiler.
claims.next_test: schema fixture proving content is absent

claims.claim: A bounded LocalContextFirewallV1 must parse raw structured configuration and is therefore part of the secrecy TCB.
A pure verifier can validate lineage and consistency but cannot authenticate a coherently lying observer or prove a parser did not leak while parsing.
At-rest encryption does not protect a namespace from a resolver process capable of decrypting that namespace.
claims.next_test: resolver compromise in a disposable namespace

claims.claim: Revocation stops future uses but cannot retract a secret already delivered to a consumer.
V1 must reject secret delivery to agent-controlled shells, arbitrary commands, and model-visible tools.
Repository policy may version an opaque required reference ID, but the reference-to-label/value mapping, leases, and audit state remain local vault state.
claims.next_test: rotation fixture showing repository policy remains resolvable without stale secret mapping

claims.claim: The accepted artifact is a design contract only and grants no live observation, secret access, lease, launch, or runtime qualification.
